title: Euler characteristics of twists by several invertible modules form a numerical polynomial
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], and let $\mathcal L_1,\ldots,\mathcal L_r$ be invertible $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-sc-invertible-module]. Then the map $(n_1,\ldots,n_r)\mapsto\chi(X,\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L_1^{\otimes n_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathcal L_r^{\otimes n_r})$ [def-pc-euler-characteristic] from $\mathbf Z^r$ to $\mathbf Z$ is a numerical polynomial in $n_1,\ldots,n_r$ of total degree at most $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension].

proof.text: Set d = dim Supp(F) and induct on d. If d = 0, every tensor product by an invertible module has the same Euler characteristic by [lem-pc-chi-zero-dim-support], so the function is constant and has degree zero.

For d > 0, note that X is of finite type over k, hence Noetherian and finite-dimensional, as the cited nodes require. Apply [lem-sc-hilbert-embedded-points] to obtain 0 \to K \to F \to F' \to 0, with equal support, no embedded associated points for F', and dim Supp(K) < d. Tensoring by every product of powers of the L_i is exact, and [lem-pc-euler-additive] reduces the assertion for F to the induction assertions for K and F'. For F', let i: Z \hookrightarrow X be the scheme-theoretic support from [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-theoretic-support]; Z is closed in X, hence proper over k. Since its annihilator kills F', [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-coherent-equivalence] gives F' \cong i_*G with G coherent and support Z; [lem-pc-closed-immersion-coherent-cohomology] identifies the Euler characteristics after tensoring with the restrictions i^*L_j. Since G is faithful on Z (the ideal of Z is the annihilator), locally O_Z embeds in a finite direct sum of copies of G, so Ass(O_Z) \subseteq Ass(G); as G has no embedded associated points and Supp(G) = Z, the scheme Z has no embedded points. Thus we may replace X,F' by Z,G: X has no embedded points, and G has no embedded associated points and support the whole scheme, of dimension d.

source.place: Tag 0BEM proof, embedded-point and scheme-theoretic-support reductions

proof.text: For the reduced situation and each index j, [lem-sc-regular-meromorphic-section-exists] (X proper, Noetherian, finite-dimensional, without embedded points) supplies a regular meromorphic section of L_j. Apply [lem-sc-hilbert-difference] to it and to the coherent module F' tensored by the other invertible powers L_i^{n_i} (i \ne j); that module still has support X and no embedded associated points, being locally isomorphic to F'. It expresses the forward difference in n_j as the difference of two Euler-characteristic functions, twisted by the same products of powers, of coherent sheaves Q, Q' with support dimension < d, to which the induction hypothesis applies.

By induction, every first difference in every coordinate is a numerical polynomial of total degree at most d - 1. The elementary arithmetic argument in Tag 0BEM integrates one coordinate difference and fixes the integration constant on the corresponding zero slice; repeating this and applying the same argument to the remaining slice gives a numerical polynomial of total degree at most d.
The induction assertion for F' together with the lower-degree assertion for K and [lem-pc-euler-additive] proves the claim for F, with total degree at most dim Supp(F).

lean.statement: theorem exists_mvPolynomial_eulerChar_tensorPowers (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] [IsProper (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] (F : X.Modules) (hF : RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace F) (r : ℕ) (L : Fin r → X.Modules) [∀ i : Fin r, (L i).IsInvertible] : ∃ P : MvPolynomial (Fin r) ℚ, (P = 0 ∨ ((P.totalDegree : ℕ∞) : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ topologicalKrullDim {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk F.val.presheaf x)}) ∧ ∀ n : Fin r → ℤ, MvPolynomial.eval (fun i => (n i : ℚ)) P = (((List.ofFn fun i : Fin r => if 0 ≤ n i then (L i).tensorPow (n i).toNat else (L i).dual.tensorPow (-n i).toNat).foldl (fun M N : X.Modules => M ⊗ N) F).eulerChar k : ℚ)
